scope: Local early-Windows terminal compatibility engineering on Windows 11 x64

results: The two release-mode desktop fixtures used separate test application identifiers. Missing helper returned an actionable error without starting a child. Two real PowerShell tabs used distinct Unicode working directories and a helper each. The active shell observed a 91x27 resize, stopped Start-Sleep with Ctrl+C and accepted the next command. The UI received exit code 23. Killing the desktop released the remaining helper and shell.

Both local Windows OpenSSH clients used the desktop terminal selection path with WinPTY. Loopback authentication failure/relogin, metadata, resize, foreground interrupt, remote disconnect, force disconnect and reconnect passed.

The original terminal smoke reproduction returned a false failure from TerminateProcess and failed to notice exit 259. The corrected release-mode smoke executable ran alongside the exact packaged helpers under a Unicode extraction path. Both automatic native ConPTY and selected WinPTY verified two shells, successful force termination, and exit code 259 on both architectures.

Each production executable ran its read-only build-info entry point. The extracted prerequisite checker recognized matching helpers and detected a missing agent. Every ZIP payload digest, architecture and upstream WinPTY file was checked.
limits: Local machine was Windows 11 x64; x86 ran under WOW64. The compatibility backend was explicitly selected on this machine. Automatic use on a system genuinely lacking ConPTY and end-to-end compatibility on early Windows 10, native x86, Arm and Windows Server still require OS acceptance.
GUI interaction ran against a release-mode host with an isolated identifier. Package entry points, hashes, helper binaries and offline checker were verified independently.
